clusters.label: Frictionless core
clusters.description: Reaches ~140 destinations without a prior visa and admits ~107 nationalities on the same terms, so it runs a mobility surplus of about 33 destinations.

clusters.label: Guarded middle (tier 2)
clusters.description: Reaches ~77 destinations without a prior visa and admits ~94 nationalities on the same terms, so it runs a mobility deficit of about 17 destinations.

clusters.label: Open but unreciprocated (tier 3)
clusters.description: Reaches ~56 destinations without a prior visa and admits ~156 nationalities on the same terms, so it runs a mobility deficit of about 100 destinations.

clusters.label: Doubly closed
clusters.description: Reaches ~47 destinations without a prior visa and admits ~18 nationalities on the same terms, so it runs a mobility surplus of about 29 destinations.

pillars.label: Economy
pillars.blurb: Can you earn, trade and transact there?

indicators.label: GDP per capita, PPP
indicators.note: Individual-level prosperity: wages, prices, standard of living.

indicators.label: GDP, PPP
indicators.note: Market size: how much economic activity the door opens onto.

indicators.label: Trade
indicators.note: How externally engaged the economy is; proxies ease of doing business as a foreigner.

pillars.label: Development
pillars.blurb: Is it a functioning, connected, modern place?

indicators.label: Human Development Index
indicators.note: UNDP composite of life expectancy, education, and income.

indicators.label: Individuals using the internet
indicators.note: Digital infrastructure; the binding constraint for remote work.

indicators.label: Tertiary school enrollment
indicators.note: Higher-education capacity; proxies value as a study destination.

pillars.label: Scale
pillars.blurb: How much world sits behind the door?

indicators.label: Surface area
indicators.note: Physical extent: how much there is to actually go and see.

pillars.label: Draw
pillars.blurb: Do people want to go — and can flights get you there?

indicators.label: International tourist arrivals
indicators.note: Revealed preference: where the world actually chooses to go.

indicators.label: International tourism receipts
indicators.note: Value, not just volume, of the tourism draw.

indicators.label: Registered carrier departures
indicators.note: Air connectivity. A visa waiver you cannot fly to is theoretical.

pillars.label: Security
pillars.blurb: Is the access safely and predictably usable?

indicators.label: Rule of law index (V-Dem)
indicators.note: Are laws applied predictably and impartially to a foreigner?

indicators.label: Electoral democracy index (V-Dem)
indicators.note: Civil-liberties environment a visitor is subject to.

indicators.label: Intentional homicides
indicators.note: Physical safety. Log-scaled: the gap from 1 to 10 per 100k matters more than 40 to 50.

pillars.label: Affordability
pillars.blurb: How far does a visitor's money go?

indicators.label: Price level (PPP-to-market exchange-rate ratio)
indicators.note: Cost of being there, relative to the world average.

lenses.label: Balanced
lenses.question: How much of the world's opportunity, on every axis at once, can you reach?

lenses.label: Business
lenses.question: How much economic activity can you show up to a meeting in?

lenses.label: Leisure
lenses.question: How much of the world worth visiting can you actually go and see?

lenses.label: Settlement
lenses.question: How much of the world could you plausibly live and work in?

lenses.label: Raw reach
lenses.question: How many people and how much output sit behind the doors you can open?
